🚨🇲🇽 <u>GRUPO MÉXICO TRAIN DERAILS, SPILLS 59,000 LITERS OF TOXIC CHEMICAL IN SONORA</u>

A Ferromex freight train — Grupo México's railroad — derailed in Naco, Sonora, spilling 59,000 liters of sodium hydrosulfide, a toxic industrial compound. President Sheinbaum said Profepa and Semarnat are already on site assessing the damage: "The measures this requires will be put in place."

Same company behind the 2014 Río Sonora spill, the worst mining disaster in Mexico's history. Twelve years later it's still paying: funds deposited, the Ures hospital under construction, and environmental remediation with Semarnat and Conagua about to start. Some debts don't expire.

🇲🇽✈️ <u>JET FUEL SPIKE COSTS MEXICAN AIRLINES 3.3BN PESOS</u>

Mexico's airlines — Volaris, Aeroméxico and Viva Aerobus — lost over 3.3 billion pesos in the second quarter as jet fuel costs jumped an average of 83%, El Financiero reports: the direct invoice of the US-Israel war on Iran landing on Mexican aviation.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>EX-PROSECUTOR PUBLICLY APOLOGIZES TO VICTIM'S FAMILY</u>

In Cancún, former prosecutor Rosa María Hernández — bound over for trial for failing the missing-persons search protocol — offered a formal public apology to the family of Francisca Mariner, the 17-year-old whose body lay unidentified in the morgue for four years. "I offer my sincerest apologies for the omissions that led to a late identification of the victim," she said. Restorative justice, applied to the officials who failed to deliver it.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>FRACKING VERDICT COMING IN TWO WEEKS</u>

Mexico's expert commission on fracking will deliver its conclusions within two weeks, Sheinbaum announced. The report was delayed precisely to bring in specialists who have long opposed unconventional gas extraction — widening the technical debate before any decision is made.

🇲🇽📱 <u>68 MILLION PHONE LINES LINKED TO ID IN MEXICO</u>

Mexico's new cellphone registry has tied 68 million lines to their users' identity — name and CURP only — to strengthen investigations of extortion and phone-based crime, digital agency chief José Antonio Peña Merino reported. Sheinbaum dismissed the surveillance narrative: the goal is fighting extortion, not controlling the population.

🇲🇽🏛️ <u>SHEINBAUM TO DECREE END OF DISCRETIONARY SECRECY</u>

Sheinbaum announced a transparency decree to stop federal agencies from withholding information at will, to be reviewed Thursday with Anticorruption Secretary Raquel Buenrostro. "Information cannot be withheld at the authority's discretion — it must be transparent, unless it is part of a judicial process," she said.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>MEXICO SHIPS MORE AID TO CUBA AND VENEZUELA</u>

One day after a massive Mexico City march against the US blockade, President Sheinbaum announced a new humanitarian aid shipment to Cuba — and two Navy vessels bound for Venezuela in the coming weeks for the victims of the June 24 earthquakes. "Sovereignty of the peoples, and whatever support we can keep giving to the people of Cuba," she said. Washington tightens the siege; Mexico sends ships.

text: 🇲🇽🏭 Mexico posts its biggest trade surplus since 1991: $9.86 billion in the first half of 2026. "Mexico's trade balance for January–June 2026 registered the largest surplus since 1991: 9,857 million dollars." — INEGI data, presented at the morning conference June alone: a $4.09 billion surplus. Exports hit $72.55 billion in the month — up 34.4% year over year. The chart shows three decades of near-unbroken deficits flipped.
